title: Fork CI reconciler: match recorded runs to a pull request, not only to its fork branch
body:
The gate tampering check (AIP-120, #74822) attributes `apache/airflow` runs to a gated pull request by head repository and branch, looking back 6 hours. Two cases are misattributed:

- A pull request that legitimately ran project CI against a base branch without the gate, then was retargeted to a gated branch within 6 hours, can be closed for tampering on the next reconciler run.
- Two open pull requests from the same fork branch (for example one to `main`, one to a release branch) share each other's runs.

Proposed: attribute runs through their recorded `pull_requests` entry (number and base) where GitHub provides it, and ignore runs recorded before the pull request's last `BaseRefChangedEvent`. Keep detection across earlier commits of the same pull request. Add tests with simultaneous pull requests from one branch, and with a retarget.

Code: `BypassFinder.find` in `dev/breeze/src/airflow_breeze/utils/fork_ci_reconcile.py`.

---
Drafted-by: Claude Code (Opus 5); reviewed by @potiuk before posting

title: Fork CI reconciler: scope the cached green-trust decision to the pull request and its base
body:
When a fork run turns green, the reconciler (AIP-120, #74822) checks once whether the pull request changes CI-defining files. It records the result as the `Fork CI / Tests (AMD)` commit status (`green` or `green_unverified`) and reuses it while that status is newer than the last retarget. A commit status belongs to the commit, so every open pull request with that head commit shares it, and their changed files can differ by base. A `green` decision made for one can mark another one ready without checking its files, which bypasses the CI-file check. The opposite case leaves a clean pull request `green_unverified`.

Proposed: key the decision by pull request and base, for example by making the status context or description specific to the base, or by recomputing when more than one open gated pull request has the same head commit. Add a test with one head commit shared by two pull requests with different bases.

Code: the green-trust block in `classify` in `dev/breeze/src/airflow_breeze/utils/fork_ci_reconcile.py`.

---
Drafted-by: Claude Code (Opus 5); reviewed by @potiuk before posting

title: Fork CI reconciler: retry a lost "push again" nudge
body:
When a gated pull request goes from `setup_required` to `awaiting_push`, the reconciler (AIP-120, #74822) edits the state comment and then posts a new comment asking the contributor to push again. If setting the status or posting that comment fails after the state comment was edited, the next run sees `awaiting_push` and never posts the nudge. The contributor gets no prompt before the inactivity closure.

Proposed: post the nudge before recording `awaiting_push` in the state comment, or record in the marker that the nudge is pending and clear it only after it was posted. Add a test where posting the nudge fails once.

Code: `classify` and `apply_plan` in `dev/breeze/src/airflow_breeze/utils/fork_ci_reconcile.py`.

title: Normalize rst license header shape and enforce it in prek
body:
### Body

The license header at the top of our `*.rst` files comes in three shapes, and the `insert-license` prek hook accepts all of them, so contributors who touch a file see a mix and guess. This surfaced in https://github.com/apache/airflow/pull/74804, where a review thread spent time on whether a leading blank line is required by the license check (it is not), and which of the existing styles is the "right" one. That is not a question a feature PR should have to answer, so this issue tracks fixing it repo-wide.

Census on `main` (`git ls-files '*.rst'`, 1759 files):

| First line of the file | Files | Example |
|---|---|---|
| ` .. Licensed to the Apache ...` (one leading space, 4-space continuation) | 1250 | `BREEZE.rst` |
| blank line, header starts on line 2 at column 0 | 356 | `providers/common/ai/docs/index.rst`, `airflow-core/docs/operators-and-hooks-ref.rst` |
| `.. Licensed to the Apache ...` at column 0 (3- or 4-space continuation) | 77 | `COMMITTERS.rst`, `providers/snowflake/docs/connections/snowflake.rst` |
| no header (newsfragments, excluded by the hook) | 76 | `airflow-core/newsfragments/*.rst` |

Why it happens: the hook (`Add license for all RST files` in `.pre-commit-config.yaml`) runs `insert-license` with `--comment-style "||"`, `--license-filepath scripts/ci/license-templates/LICENSE.rst` and `--fuzzy-match-generates-todo`. When it inserts a header it writes the first shape (verified: a fresh file gets ` .. Licensed ...` with a leading space). When a file already carries any of the three shapes, the fuzzy match passes and nothing is rewritten, so the variants never converge. Verified on the file from the PR above: the hook reports `Passed` both with and without the leading blank line.

Proposal:

1. Pick one canonical shape. The hook's own output (` .. Licensed ...`, 4-space continuation) is the natural choice because new files get it automatically; `scripts/ci/license-templates/LICENSE.rst` and `contributing-docs/08_static_code_checks.rst` should state it.
2. One mechanical PR that rewrites the 433 non-canonical files (356 blank-first-line + 77 column-0). The header is an rst comment, so rendered docs do not change. Doing it in one go, or one PR per top-level area, keeps the conflict window short for open PRs.
3. Make the check strict so the shapes cannot drift again: either drop `--fuzzy-match-generates-todo` for rst (so a non-exact header is treated as missing and the hook rewrites it), or add a small prek script that fails when an rst file's header does not start on line 1 with the canonical text.

Acceptance criteria: every tracked `*.rst` outside the hook's exclusions starts with the identical canonical header on line 1, and the static check fails on a file that deviates.

title: Language SDK task state writes skip the max_value_storage_bytes warning
body:
### Description

`[state_store] max_value_storage_bytes` caps the size of a task state value. The public REST API rejects an oversized value with a 422, and a Python task logs a warning and still writes the value (`task-sdk/src/airflow/sdk/execution_time/context.py`), so a running task is never failed over the size.

Tasks run by the Go, TypeScript and Java SDKs get neither, because:

- the coordinator does not pass `max_value_storage_bytes` to the language SDK
  runtime (`_build_runtime_env()` in
  `task-sdk/src/airflow/sdk/coordinators/_subprocess.py` passes only
  `default_retention_days` from `[state_store]`), and
- neither the supervisor nor the Execution API checks the size on the write path.

Proposed change:

1. Have the coordinator pass the setting as `AIRFLOW__STATE_STORE__MAX_VALUE_STORAGE_BYTES`, as it already does for 
   `AIRFLOW__STATE_STORE__DEFAULT_RETENTION_DAYS`.
2. In each SDK's task state `Set`, measure the value the way Python does    (`len(json.dumps(value))`, which is also the length of the string the Execution API stores) and log a warning when it is over a positive limit. The write still proceeds.
3. When the variable is not set, skip the check rather than fail the write. This covers an older coordinator that does not pass it.

### Use case/motivation

An operator sets `max_value_storage_bytes` to steer task state toward small coordination values. A Python task that writes more gets a warning in its log; a Go, TypeScript or Java task writing the same value gets nothing. On Postgres and SQLite the value column has no practical size limit, so the value is stored without anyone noticing. On MySQL (`MEDIUMTEXT`) the write fails at around 16 MB.

### Related issues

Each SDK already has a TODO for this, added during review of the task state store PRs: Go in #73420, Java in #73464 and TypeScript in #73618. #74400 tracks a related language SDK state store gap (`[workers] state_store_backend`).

I have the coordinator and Go SDK change ready; TypeScript and Java would follow in separate PRs.

title: GET /api/v2/dags queries dag_tag during response serialization, on the API server's event loop (follow-up to #74239)
body:
### Under which category would you file this issue?

Airflow Core

### Apache Airflow version

3.3.2 (the code is unchanged on main as of 2026-10-18; line numbers below are 3.3.2's)

### What happened?

#74239 and #74247 fixed two responses that queried the database inside `dump_json`, on the event loop: `get_dag_details` and `get_pools`. `GET /api/v2/dags` does the same.

`generate_dag_with_latest_run_query` adds `selectinload(DagModel.tags)` (`api_fastapi/common/db/dags.py:49`). The route returns the un-iterated `ScalarResult` (`dags = session.scalars(dags_select)`, `core_api/routes/public/dags.py:178`) into `dags: Iterable[DAGResponse]` (`core_api/datamodels/dags.py:173`), which pydantic validates lazily. So the selectin query on `dag_tag` runs while FastAPI 0.136.3 serializes the response on the loop (`fastapi/routing.py:292-306`: validation in the threadpool, serialization on the loop).

The query uses the route's own connection, because function-scoped dependencies exit after serialization (`fastapi/routing.py:118-121`). While it waits (on a lock, a slow disk or a busy server), the process answers nothing else, including `/execution/health/ping` and `/api/v2/monitor/health`.

With `dag_tag` locked for 60 s and one `GET /api/v2/dags` in flight (commands under *How to reproduce*). `t` is seconds from taking the lock; the listing was sent at t+2s:

```
before: ping 200 2.696615s | health 200 0.005201s | dags 200 0.023518s
t+3s:  ping 000 3.001651s | health 000 3.002222s
t+10s: ping 000 3.002274s | health 000 3.002221s
t+17s: ping 000 3.002221s | health 000 3.002275s
t+24s: ping 000 3.002732s | health 000 3.002301s
t+31s: ping 000 3.002335s | health 000 3.002271s
t+38s: ping 000 3.002375s | health 000 3.002221s
t+45s: ping 000 3.002259s | health 000 3.002239s
t+52s: ping 000 3.002253s | health 000 3.002248s
t+59s: ping 200 0.907544s | health 200 0.005766s
t+61s: ping 200 0.002542s | health 200 0.005371s
GET /api/v2/dags: 200 after 58.041028s
```

As a control, the same lock with `GET /api/v2/pools` in flight (which reads no `dag_tag`) gives `pools 200 0.026610s`, and ping and health answer in 2-6 ms throughout.

The api-server's main thread during the hold (`py-spy dump`, t+~10s):

```
Thread 2414 (idle): "MainThread"
    do_execute (sqlalchemy/engine/default.py:952)
    _exec_single_context (sqlalchemy/engine/base.py:1969)
    _execute_context (sqlalchemy/engine/base.py:1848)
    _execute_clauseelement (sqlalchemy/engine/base.py:1643)
    _execute_on_connection (sqlalchemy/sql/elements.py:526)
    execute (sqlalchemy/engine/base.py:1421)
    orm_execute_statement (sqlalchemy/orm/context.py:306)
    _execute_internal (sqlalchemy/orm/session.py:2271)
    execute (sqlalchemy/orm/session.py:2373)
    _load_via_parent (sqlalchemy/orm/strategies.py:3426)
    _load_for_path (sqlalchemy/orm/strategies.py:3350)
    invoke (sqlalchemy/orm/loading.py:1564)
    chunks (sqlalchemy/orm/loading.py:247)
    iterrows (sqlalchemy/engine/result.py:566)
    dump_json (pydantic/type_adapter.py:677)
    serialize_json (fastapi/_compat/v2.py:231)
    serialize_response (fastapi/routing.py:306)
    app (fastapi/routing.py:695)
    app (fastapi/routing.py:120)
    wrapped_app (starlette/_exception_handler.py:42)
    ...
    run (uvicorn/server.py:77)
    _run_api_server_with_uvicorn (airflow/cli/commands/api_server_command.py:138)
Thread 2455 (idle): "AnyIO worker thread"
    wait (threading.py:355)
    get (queue.py:171)
    run (anyio/_backends/_asyncio.py:1089)
```

Where the same request checks connections out, with no lock, using the checkout listener from the script in #74239 on `create_app("core")`:

```
GET /api/v2/dags -> 200, total_entries 1, checkouts 3, on the event loop 1
    [event loop] core_api/security.py:155 get_user > core_api/security.py:126 resolve_user_from_token > ... (is_revoked, #66493)
    [AnyIO worker thread] core_api/security.py:368 depends_permitted_dags_filter > ... base_auth_manager.py:588 get_authorized_dag_ids
    [AnyIO worker thread] core_api/routes/public/dags.py:152 get_dags > ... common/db/common.py:197 paginated_select > utils/db.py:1762 get_query_count
```

The `dag_tag` query is not among the checkouts, because it runs on the connection the route already holds. A checkout listener therefore does not show this case; a statement listener, or a stack dump as above, does.

### What you think should happen instead?

Response serialization should not query the database. A slow or locked `dag_tag` should then slow `GET /api/v2/dags` only, not every request the process serves.

Materialise the rows in the route, inside the threadpool: `session.scalars(dags_select).all()`, as `patch_dags` already does, or `dags: list[DAGResponse]`, as #74247 did for pools. Then the selectin query runs while the route builds the response.

**Scope (from reading 3.3.2; only `get_dags` reproduced).**
- 19 response fields in `core_api/datamodels` (16 files) are typed `Iterable[...]`, plus 2 in `execution_api/datamodels`.
- 13 route handlers assign a bare `session.scalars(...)` result instead of calling `.all()`: 12 in the core API and 1 in the Execution API.
- Any of these whose rows load a relationship, or read a lazy attribute while they are produced, will query on the loop the same way. `pools` was one of them before #74247.

A blanket alternative is to serialize sync endpoints in the threadpool, the same place FastAPI already validates them (`fastapi/routing.py:292-297`). We run that as a workaround; it keeps the loop free, but each response then holds a threadpool slot while it serializes.

### How to reproduce

Environment: unmodified `apache-airflow[postgres]==3.3.2` on the 3.3.2 constraints, Python 3.12.3, PostgreSQL 16.15, Ubuntu 24.04. `airflow api-server` runs with its defaults (uvicorn, 1 worker).

```bash
export AIRFLOW_HOME=/tmp/repro
export AIRFLOW__DATABASE__SQL_ALCHEMY_CONN=postgresql+psycopg2://postgres:test@127.0.0.1:5432/postgres
export AIRFLOW__CORE__DAGS_FOLDER=/tmp/repro/dags AIRFLOW__CORE__LOAD_EXAMPLES=False
export AIRFLOW__CORE__AUTH_MANAGER=airflow.api_fastapi.auth.managers.simple.simple_auth_manager.SimpleAuthManager
export AIRFLOW__CORE__SIMPLE_AUTH_MANAGER_ALL_ADMINS=True
export AIRFLOW__API_AUTH__JWT_SECRET=$(python -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_hex(32))")
mkdir -p /tmp/repro/dags
cat > /tmp/repro/dags/tagged.py <<'EOF'
from airflow.sdk import DAG, task

with DAG("tagged", schedule=None, tags=["example"]):

    @task
    def noop():
        pass

    noop()
EOF
airflow db migrate && airflow dags reserialize
airflow api-server --port 8080 &
```

Get a token with `get_auth_manager().generate_jwt(SimpleAuthManagerUser(username="admin", role="admin"))`, as in the script in #74239. Then:

```bash
# session 1: hold dag_tag for 60 s
psql -c "BEGIN; LOCK TABLE dag_tag IN ACCESS EXCLUSIVE MODE; SELECT pg_sleep(60); COMMIT;" &
sleep 2
# session 2: one listing
curl -s -o /dev/null -w 'GET /api/v2/dags: %{http_code} after %{time_total}s\n' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/v2/dags &
# session 3: the probes, 3 s timeout each
curl -s -o /dev/null -m 3 -w '%{http_code} %{time_total}s\n' http://127.0.0.1:8080/execution/health/ping
curl -s -o /dev/null -m 3 -w '%{http_code} %{time_total}s\n' http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/v2/monitor/health
```

### Operating System

Ubuntu 24.04 (Linux 6.17), Python 3.12.3

### Versions of Apache Airflow Providers

`apache-airflow-providers-postgres` 7.0.2 (the `postgres` extra) and the providers `apache-airflow` 3.3.2 installs by default, all at the versions pinned by `constraints-3.3.2/constraints-3.12.txt`. The reproduction uses none of them beyond the PostgreSQL driver.

### Deployment

Other

### Deployment details

`pip install "apache-airflow[postgres]==3.3.2"` with the 3.3.2 constraints, and `airflow api-server` started directly (uvicorn, 1 worker), against PostgreSQL 16.15. FastAPI 0.136.3, Starlette 1.6.0, pydantic 2.13.5 (pydantic-core 2.46.5), SQLAlchemy 2.0.52, uvicorn 0.52.4, anyio 4.15.1, psycopg2-binary 2.9.13.

### Anything else?

The same pattern exists elsewhere in the code (the scope list above), but only `get_dags` has been reproduced. The one checkout on the loop in the listing above is `is_revoked`, which is #66493 / #73422, not this issue.

title: template_fields_extra as frozenset has non-deterministic iteration order across processes
body:
### Summary

`BaseOperator.template_fields_extra` is typed `ClassVar[frozenset[str]]`. The PR that introduces it (apache/airflow#74920) iterates that value in three places to build the merged `template_fields` tuple and the `MappedOperator.template_fields_extra` value. **`frozenset` iteration order is not stable across Python processes** — string hashing in CPython 3.3+ is randomized per process via `PYTHONHASHSEED`. The result is a different `template_fields_extra` / merged `template_fields` order in the Dag processor, scheduler, worker, and tests, and a different serialized value in the metadata DB on every parse.

### Reproduce

```text
$ for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do python3 -c "print(tuple(frozenset({'alpha','beta','gamma'})))"; done
('gamma', 'beta', 'alpha')
('beta', 'alpha', 'gamma')
('alpha', 'gamma', 'beta')
('gamma', 'alpha', 'beta')
('beta', 'gamma', 'alpha')
```

### Where it bites in the existing PR

- `task-sdk/src/airflow/sdk/bases/operator.py:1269-1271` — `BaseOperator.__init__` does `*type(self).template_fields_extra` (a `frozenset`); the merged `template_fields` order depends on the process.
- `task-sdk/src/airflow/sdk/definitions/mappedoperator.py:254-262` — `OperatorPartial.__call__` does `tuple(dict.fromkeys((*self.operator_class.template_fields, *self.operator_class.template_fields_extra)))` and `template_fields_extra=tuple(self.operator_class.template_fields_extra)`. The order flows into `MappedOperator.template_fields` and `template_fields_extra`.
- `task-sdk/src/airflow/sdk/bases/decorator.py:723-732` — same shape on the `@task` decorator path.
- `airflow-core/src/airflow/serialization/serialized_objects.py:1373` — the resulting tuple is written into `SerializedBaseOperator.template_fields_extra` and persisted.
- `airflow-core/src/airflow/serialization/dag_version_diff.py:268` — `template_fields_extra` is one of the fields the diff uses to compute the next serialized Dag version, so order drift between parses triggers spurious Dag-version churn.

### Concrete test failures

- `task-sdk/tests/task_sdk/bases/test_operator.py::TestTemplateFieldsExtra::test_template_fields_extra_preserves_order_and_deduplicates` asserts a deterministic order from `frozenset({"arg2", "arg3"})`; that assertion only holds in processes whose `PYTHONHASHSEED` happens to iterate the set in that order. Running under a different seed flips the list to `["arg1", "arg3", "arg2"]` and the test fails.
- `test_template_fields_extra_preserves_order_and_deduplicates_through_mapped_operator` asserts the same property through `.partial().expand()` and is similarly seed-dependent.
- The serialization tests in `airflow-core/tests/unit/serialization/test_dag_serialization.py` already work around the instability: `test_serialize_template_fields_extra_roundtrip` (line 2096) and `test_serialize_template_fields_extra_roundtrip_mapped` use `sorted()` / `set()` on the result. The author of the PR felt the instability and patched the test instead of fixing the data type.

### Why this contradicts the new docstring

`task-sdk/src/airflow/sdk/bases/operator.py:954-959`:

> Additional fields, declared by subclasses, that should be rendered with Jinja and treated as `XComArg` capable in addition to `template_fields`. Use this for string fields that are intentionally not promoted into `template_fields` but still need to receive XCom references (such as `some_task.output`) from upstream tasks.

The docstring promises a deterministic, declared order; `frozenset[str]` cannot deliver either. The merge in `__init__` is described as `dict.fromkeys((*self.template_fields, *extra))` "preserving order, deduplicating" — but `*extra` over a `frozenset` does not preserve any user-declared order at all.

### Impact

- Spurious Dag-version diffs on every reparse when the seed rolls differently between processes. This is the same class of bug as the recently-closed apache/airflow#53957 ("`@task.kubernetes` decorator causes different dag hash on every serialized dag update").
- `MappedOperator.template_fields_extra` and the merged `template_fields` are written to the metadata DB; reading them back across processes yields a tuple that may not match the in-memory object.
- The order of fields in the rendered-template UI table for any operator that opts in is process-dependent.

### Suggested fix

1. Change `BaseOperator.template_fields_extra` to `ClassVar[Sequence[str]] = ()`. Accept `tuple`, `list`, or `frozenset`; document the supported types and the fact that declaration order is what is preserved.
2. Stop materialising `tuple(self.operator_class.template_fields_extra)`; instead, cast / coerce to `tuple` while preserving the source order. Same change in `OperatorPartial.__call__`, `_TaskDecorator`, and the `BaseOperator.__init__` merge.
3. Tighten `MappedOperator.template_fields_extra` and `SerializedBaseOperator.template_fields_extra` to `Sequence[str]` so the contract is explicit in the type.
4. Update the order/dedup tests so they feed an ordered `tuple` and assert that order verbatim. The `frozenset` cases should be either dropped or rewritten to assert only the set, not the order.
5. Add a regression test that re-runs the order-preservation assertion in a subprocess with `PYTHONHASHSEED=random` so a future change cannot silently make the order seed-dependent again.

### Environment

- Reproduced on macOS, CPython 3.14.7.
- Discovered while reviewing apache/airflow#74920.

title: Asset timetable deserializes batch_asset_events to True when key absent, contradicting the opt-in False default
body:
### Apache Airflow version

3.4.0b1 (v3-4-test)

### What happened

An asset-triggered timetable deserializes `batch_asset_events` to **`True`** when the key is absent from the serialized data, but the authoring/config default is **`False`** (asset-event batching is opt-in, added in #68517). So any serialized DAG whose blob lacks the key — every DAG serialized before 3.4, and the transient window after upgrade before the dag-processor re-parses — comes back with `batch_asset_events=True`, silently batching queued asset events into a single DAG run instead of one run per event.

The three deserialize sites all hardcode the `True` fallback:
- `airflow-core/src/airflow/timetables/simple.py:251` (`AssetTriggeredTimetable`)
- `airflow-core/src/airflow/timetables/simple.py:465` (`PartitionedAssetTimetable`)
- `airflow-core/src/airflow/timetables/assets.py:71` (`AssetOrTimeSchedule`)

whereas the attrs field default is `attrs.Factory(_get_default_batch_asset_events)` which returns `conf.getboolean("scheduler", "batch_asset_events", fallback=False) or get_batching_requirement() is not None` — i.e. `False` for a plain asset condition.

### What you think should happen instead

Deserializing a blob without the key should yield the same value as authoring the timetable — `False` for a plain condition (and `True` for AND/partition conditions, which *require* batching). I.e. the absent-key fallback should defer to the construct-time factory default, not a hardcoded `True`.

### How to reproduce

```python
from airflow.sdk import Asset
from airflow.timetables.simple import AssetTriggeredTimetable

tt = AssetTriggeredTimetable(assets=Asset("x"))
print(tt.batch_asset_events)                       # False  (opt-in default)

legacy_blob = {"asset_condition": tt.serialize()["asset_condition"]}   # key omitted
restored = AssetTriggeredTimetable.deserialize(legacy_blob)
print(restored.batch_asset_events)                 # True   <-- bug
```

Confirmed on v3-4-test. A normal round-trip (`deserialize(tt.serialize())`, key present) correctly returns `False`.

### Suggested fix

At each deserialize site, only pass `batch_asset_events` when the key is present so the attrs factory default applies when it is absent. A hardcoded `False` is **not** correct because AND-condition / partitioned timetables require batching (`True`).

### Are you willing to submit PR?

Yes.

### Operating System / Deployment / Versions

v3-4-test branch (3.4.0).

title: KubernetesPodOperator startup event polling overloads kube-apiserver at scale and fails tasks on 504
body:
### Under which category would you file this issue?

Providers

### Apache Airflow version

3.2.0 (constraints pin `apache-airflow-providers-cncf-kubernetes==10.14.0`). The affected code path is unchanged on `main`.

### What happened and how to reproduce it?

Since `apache-airflow-providers-cncf-kubernetes` 10.6.0 (#50192), the synchronous `KubernetesPodOperator` starts a background event watcher while it waits for the pod to leave `Pending`. `PodManager.watch_pod_events` calls `list_namespaced_event(namespace, field_selector="involvedObject.name=<pod>")` every `startup_check_interval_seconds` (default 5 s) for every running task. Before 10.6.0 (for example 8.3.3, pinned by Airflow 2.9.3) the startup loop only issued `read_namespaced_pod`, a cheap GET by name.

Two problems follow from this on a large, volatile cluster (reported at ~10 000 concurrent Airflow + Spark pods on EKS 1.36 with the official Helm chart):

1. **The event LIST is expensive and scales with the namespace, not with the pod.** kube-apiserver disables the watch cache for `Event` objects by default (`DefaultWatchCacheSizes` in `pkg/kubeapiserver/default_storage_factory_builder.go` sets `events` and `events.k8s.io/events` to 0), and etcd has no secondary indexes, so every event LIST, with or without `resourceVersion`, is an etcd range read of the whole namespace event prefix followed by field-selector filtering in the API server. With thousands of pods, a one-hour event TTL and ~5–8 events per pod, each call reads and filters hundreds of thousands of objects, multiplied by every starting task every 5 s. The apiserver request timeout trips and the client sees:

   ```
   WARNING - Retrying airflow.providers.cncf.kubernetes.utils.pod_manager.PodManager.read_pod_events in 8 seconds as it raised ApiException: (504)
   Reason: Gateway Timeout
   HTTP response body: {"metadata":{},"status":"Failure","message":"Timeout: request did not complete within the allotted timeout","reason":"Timeout","details":{},"code":504}
   ```

   Because the watch cache is off for Events, the `resourceVersion` / `NotOlderThan` optimisations from #59080 and #66471 do not reduce this cost on a default cluster; they only help on clusters that enable an Event watch cache through `--watch-cache-sizes`.

2. **A failure of the event watcher fails the task even though the pod is fine.** `KubernetesPodOperator.await_pod_start` runs the watcher as an `asyncio` task and, in its `finally` block, does `events_task.cancel()` followed by `await events_task` with only `CancelledError` suppressed. When the watcher has already died with `ApiException` after the `[workers] api_retries` attempts, that `await` re-raises it, `asyncio.run` propagates it, and the task fails. Logging events during startup is a convenience; it should never decide the task outcome. The one-shot read behind `log_events_on_failure` already uses `_optionally_suppress(reraise=False)`; the startup watcher does not.

There is no configuration or operator parameter that disables the startup event watcher. `log_events_on_failure` only controls the one-shot read after a failure. `SparkKubernetesOperator` inherits the same behaviour.

Reproduction without a 10 000-pod cluster: make `list_namespaced_event` raise `ApiException(status=504)` (for example with a mock, or an RBAC/admission rule that rejects event lists) and run any `KubernetesPodOperator` task with `deferrable=False`. The pod starts and completes, yet the task fails with the `ApiException` once the retries are exhausted.

Workaround until this is fixed (the loop in `PodManager.watch_pod_events` checks `stop_watching_events` before every poll):

```python
class QuietKubernetesPodOperator(KubernetesPodOperator):
    def await_pod_start(self, pod):
        self.pod_manager.stop_watching_events = True
        super().await_pod_start(pod)
```

Other mitigations: raise `startup_check_interval_seconds`, keep Spark executor pods in a separate namespace from operator pods (the scan cost is per namespace), or use `deferrable=True` (the triggerer uses a watch stream instead of polling lists).

### What you think should happen instead?

1. The startup event watcher must be best-effort: an API error after retries should log one warning and stop watching, while pod start tracking continues and the task outcome stays unaffected.
2. `KubernetesPodOperator` (and `KubernetesPodTrigger`) should expose an opt-out for the startup event watcher, mirroring `log_events_on_failure`, so users on large clusters can disable it without subclassing.

### Operating System

Linux (EKS nodes)

### Deployment

Official Apache Airflow Helm Chart

### Apache Airflow Provider(s)

cncf-kubernetes

### Versions of Apache Airflow Providers

`apache-airflow-providers-cncf-kubernetes>=10.6.0` (introduced by #50192). Verified on 10.14.0 and on `main`.

### Kubernetes Version

1.36 (EKS). The disabled watch cache for `Event` objects is the default on every Kubernetes version.

### Anything else?

Related work that improved but did not remove the cost: #59080 (adds `resourceVersion` / `NotOlderThan`, motivated by the same "many pods started in parallel" load), #60532 (async watch reconnects), #66470 / #66471 (seed `resourceVersion` after an empty list, released in 10.17.1), #58736 (403 on event list, fixed by chart RBAC in #56872). None of them adds an opt-out or makes the watcher best-effort.

### Are you willing to submit PR?

- [X] Yes I am willing to submit a PR!

---

title: Forward log_events_on_startup to the GKE and EKS deferrable pod triggers
body:
### Description

#75013 adds `log_events_on_startup` to `KubernetesPodOperator` and `KubernetesPodTrigger` so users on large clusters can switch off the startup event watcher, which makes the API server read every event in the namespace on each poll.

The GKE and EKS operators inherit the synchronous path, so the parameter works there in sync mode. In deferrable mode it is lost:

- `GKEStartPodOperator.invoke_defer_method` (`providers/google/src/airflow/providers/google/cloud/operators/kubernetes_engine.py`) builds `GKEStartPodTrigger` with an explicit kwarg list that does not include the flag, and `GKEStartPodTrigger.serialize()` re-lists its fields without it.
- `EksPodOperator.invoke_defer_method` (`providers/amazon/src/airflow/providers/amazon/aws/operators/eks.py`) builds `EksPodTrigger` the same way, and `EksPodTrigger.__init__` has a fixed signature with no `**kwargs`.

`KubernetesPodTrigger.serialize()` therefore emits the key only when the flag is `False`, so neither subclass breaks, but `GKEStartPodOperator(deferrable=True, log_events_on_startup=False)` and the EKS equivalent still watch events in the triggerer. The provider docs (`providers/cncf/kubernetes/docs/operators.rst`, "Pod events in the task log") state this limitation.

### Work needed

1. Forward `log_events_on_startup` from both operators to their triggers.
2. Accept and serialize it in `EksPodTrigger` and include it in `GKEStartPodTrigger.serialize()` (only when `False`, matching the base trigger).
3. Raise the `apache-airflow-providers-cncf-kubernetes` minimum version in the google and amazon providers to the release that ships the parameter; the trigger `__init__` of older cncf versions rejects the kwarg.
4. Remove the limitation sentence from the cncf docs.

### Acceptance criteria

- `GKEStartPodOperator(deferrable=True, log_events_on_startup=False)` and `EksPodOperator(deferrable=True, log_events_on_startup=False)` create no event watch in the triggerer (unit test on each trigger's `_wait_for_pod_start`).
- Default serialization of both triggers stays unchanged.

### Related

- #75013
- #75016 (the cncf change that introduces the parameter)

title: Task supervisor raises TypeError when a task log event has a key named target or msg, orphaning the task process and recording a successful task as failed
body:
### Under which category would you file this issue?

Task SDK

### Apache Airflow version

main (development), reproduced at d2c41b8c2027fcba5e632f00f5f80d86ec767981. Also 3.3.2 with apache-airflow-task-sdk 1.3.2 and 3.4.0b1 with task-sdk 1.4.0b1, which carry the same helper. 3.3.1 and task-sdk 1.3.1 are not affected.

### What happened and how to reproduce it?

`process_log_messages_from_subprocess` in `task-sdk/src/airflow/sdk/execution_time/supervisor.py` (lines 2909-2921) pops `level`, `event` and `exception` from each JSON log event coming from the task process and spreads every other key into the helper `_log_to_target(target, level, msg, **event)` (line 2913, defined at line 2916). A log event that carries a key named `target` or `msg` collides with the helper's own parameter names and raises:

```
TypeError: _log_to_target() got multiple values for argument 'target'
```

Nothing on the way out catches it: `make_buffered_socket_reader.cb` catches only `StopIteration`, `_service_subprocess` only `BrokenPipeError` and `ConnectionResetError`, `ActivitySubprocess.wait` has only a `finally` that closes the selector, `_PythonCoordinator.execute_task` has no handler and `supervise_task` catches only `TaskLaunchError` and httpx request errors. So `wait()` raises before `update_task_state_if_needed()` and `_upload_logs()`, the heartbeat loop stops, and the child, which runs in its own process group, is not killed.

An ordinary log call in a task is enough:

```python
structlog.get_logger().info("deploying", target="prod")
```

Airflow itself supplies a second trigger. `task_runner.py` line 1239 logs `log.debug("Using serialized startup message from environment", msg=msg)` in the `run_as_user` re-exec path, and debug events are forwarded to the supervisor when `[logging] logging_level = DEBUG`. So every impersonated task in a DEBUG-logging deployment should hit this with no Dag author involvement (the debug forwarding of a `msg=` key was reproduced; the `sudo` re-exec itself was not run).

Observed on the checkout, driving `supervise_task` with a real forked child and a mock API transport that records every request:

```
info("deploying", target="prod")   -> supervise_task raised TypeError after 0.35 s
   requests sent: PATCH .../run, one PUT .../heartbeat; no state PATCH, no log upload
   child not killed: ran user code to the end, then its terminal message failed with
   ConnectionResetError; pid still present 9 s after the supervisor raised
info("deploying", msg="prod")      -> same, "multiple values for argument 'msg'"
debug("deploying", msg="prod")     -> rc 0 at logging_level=INFO, TypeError at DEBUG
info("deploying", environment="prod") -> rc 0, PATCH .../state {"state": "success"}
```

Under the standard executors the task instance does not stay running until the heartbeat timeout: the LocalExecutor worker reports the workload's failure state and the Celery wrapper re-raises, so the scheduler's `process_executor_events` sees a failed event for a running task instance, logs a state mismatch, counts `tasks.killed_externally` and calls `handle_failure` (read from the code, the executor and scheduler were not run). The result is that a task whose user code succeeds is recorded as failed or up for retry, a retry can start while the orphaned process is still running user code, and the task's final logs are never uploaded.

The same generator serves the Dag processor: `DagFileProcessorProcess` registers it through `WatchedSubprocess._register_pipe_readers`, and `DagFileProcessorManager._service_processor_sockets` (`airflow-core/src/airflow/dag_processing/manager.py` lines 636-639) catches only the same two socket errors while `DagProcessorJobRunner._execute` logs and re-raises. A Dag file with `structlog.get_logger().info("parse", target="prod")` at module level, run under `DagFileProcessorProcess.start`, raised the same `TypeError` from the processor's selector callback; from the code, that stops the Dag processor job and does so again on every restart.

The helper was added by #69523 (6d9cc2ed37) and backported by #72888 (3b6f63eef9). Before it, the code called `target.log(level, msg, **event)` directly, where only `level` and `event` could collide and both are popped.

**How to reproduce**

1. A Dag with a Python task whose callable runs `structlog.get_logger().info("deploying", target="prod")` and then sleeps a few seconds.
2. Run it under the task SDK supervisor (any executor).
3. The supervisor logs the `TypeError` above and exits without sending a terminal state; the task process keeps running; the task instance is then failed by the scheduler's state-mismatch handling.

For the Dag processor: put the same log call at module level in a Dag file and watch the Dag processor stop.

### What you think should happen instead?

A log event's keys should never be able to collide with the forwarding helper's parameters. Making them positional-only removes both collisions:

```python
def _log_to_target(target, level, msg, /, **event):
```

Alternatively pass the event as one dict and call `target.log(level, msg, **event)` inside. The existing `test_process_log_messages_from_subprocess` sends only `level` and `event`; a case with `{"level": "info", "event": "x", "target": "y", "msg": "z"}` would cover this.

### Operating System

Linux

Other

With `[logging] logging_level = DEBUG` and `run_as_user` set, the startup debug line in `task_runner.py` (line 1239) carries `msg=` and should trigger the same crash for every impersonated task.

title: Breeze: check-translation-completeness key order conflicts with the UI ESLint rule
body:
### What happened and how to reproduce it?

`breeze ui check-translation-completeness --add-missing` / `--remove-unused` rewrites each locale file with its keys sorted by `natural_sort_key()` (`dev/breeze/src/airflow_breeze/commands/ui_commands.py`), which compares case-insensitively. The repo enforces a different order for the same files: `jsonc/sort-keys` with `natural: true` (`airflow-core/src/airflow/ui/rules/jsonc.js`), applied by the `ts-compile-lint-ui` pre-commit hook. eslint-plugin-jsonc (3.4.2 here) implements that rule with `natural-compare`, which is case-sensitive — uppercase letters sort before lowercase ones.

Both write helpers sort the whole file, not just the added/removed keys, so any locale file that gets rewritten (it has to have missing or unused keys to be touched at all) can be re-ordered as a side effect. For case-dependent keys the resulting order violates the repo's own ESLint rule, and the pre-commit hook flips those keys back — pure churn for contributors.

Observed while updating the zh-TW locale (#75061, merged): the command reordered 4 pre-existing key pairs and the `Compile / format / lint UI` hook reverted all of them:

| keys | order written by breeze | order required by ESLint |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `logLevel` / `logicalDate` | `logicalDate`, `logLevel` | `logLevel`, `logicalDate` |
| `selectLanguage` / `selected` | `selected`, `selectLanguage` | `selectLanguage`, `selected` |
| `sortMultiColumnHint` / `sortedAscending` | `sortedAscending`, `sortMultiColumnHint` | `sortMultiColumnHint`, `sortedAscending` |
| `modeTooltip` / `modes` | `modes`, `modeTooltip` | `modeTooltip`, `modes` |

Minimal check of the ESLint side (from `airflow-core/src/airflow/ui`):

```console
$ cat public/i18n/locales/en/scratch.json   # order as written by the breeze command
{
  "logicalDate": "Logical Date",
  "logLevel": "Log Level"
}
$ pnpm exec eslint public/i18n/locales/en/scratch.json
  2:3  error  Expected object keys to be in natural ascending order. 'logicalDate' should be after 'logLevel'  jsonc/sort-keys

✖ 1 problem (1 error, 0 warnings)
```

`pnpm exec eslint --fix` rewrites the file with `"logLevel"` first.

Tool side, with the committed `natural_sort_key`:

```pycon
>>> from airflow_breeze.commands.ui_commands import natural_sort_key
>>> sorted(["logLevel", "logicalDate"], key=natural_sort_key)
['logicalDate', 'logLevel']
>>> sorted(["selectLanguage", "selected"], key=natural_sort_key)
['selected', 'selectLanguage']
```

### What you think should happen instead?

The command should write keys in the order the repo enforces, so that using it never produces an order ESLint rejects. Options:

1. Align `natural_sort_key()` with the comparator the rule actually uses: port the character mapping of `natural-compare` (case-sensitive — digits before letters, `A-Z` before `a-z`, same punctuation mapping) and update `TestNaturalSorting.test_natural_sort_matches_eslint` accordingly. The current docstring says the key "mimics JavaScript's `localeCompare` with `numeric: true`" — eslint-plugin-jsonc does not use `localeCompare`; it depends on `natural-compare`.
2. Or run the UI ESLint fix step on the rewritten files (e.g. invoke the existing `ts-compile-lint-ui` hook, or `pnpm eslint --fix`, from the command). That was the plan agreed in #58487 when it was closed ("convert `check_translation_completeness` into a breeze command and run prek run eslint as part of it") — the conversion landed (#58637), but the command writes its own order and never invokes ESLint.

For completeness, the rule also supports `caseSensitive: false`; enabling it would make ESLint accept the current tool order, but every existing locale file would then have to be re-sorted, so aligning the command is likely the cheaper fix.

### Anything else?

- Related history: #58487 reported this churn for the previous script and was closed assuming the new breeze command would run ESLint. The conversion to a breeze command (#58637) introduced the current comparator, but ESLint is still not invoked — this issue tracks what remains.
- `TestNaturalSorting.test_natural_sort_matches_eslint` currently locks in the wrong expectation: it asserts `Zebra` sorts last, while `natural-compare` sorts `Z` (mapped to 101) before `a` (mapped to 102), i.e. `Zebra` first — ESLint reports "Expected object keys to be in natural ascending order. 'apple' should be after 'Zebra'". The test needs to be updated together with the comparator.

title: RedactedIO leaks secret bytes to stdout
body:
### Describe the bug

`RedactedIO.write()` and `RedactedIO.writelines()` are supposed to mask registered secrets before any output reaches the terminal. They do — for `str` values. For `bytes` (and `bytearray`) values, the registered secret is written to stdout in cleartext, wrapped in Python's `bytes` repr (`b'…'`).

The only production call site today is `airflow tasks test` ([`airflow-core/src/airflow/cli/commands/task_command.py:539`](https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/main/airflow-core/src/airflow/cli/commands/task_command.py#L539)), which wraps task execution in `redirect_stdout(RedactedIO())`. Any task that calls `sys.stdout.writelines([b"…secret…"])` — common with subprocess wrappers, log buffers, and some logging libraries — will have its secrets printed verbatim.

### Reproducer

```python
from airflow.sdk._shared.secrets_masker import mask_secret, RedactedIO

mask_secret("hunter2")

# str — masked
RedactedIO().write("here is hunter2")
# -> here is ***

# bytes containing the same secret — NOT masked
RedactedIO().write(b"here is hunter2")
# -> b'here is hunter2'   <-- secret leaked as bytes repr
```

Equivalently, after the `airflow tasks test` wrapper is active inside a Dag:

```python
import sys
def my_task(**_):
    sys.stdout.writelines([b"authorization: Bearer hunter2\n"])
    # Writes "authorization: Bearer b'authorization: Bearer hunter2\n'"
    # to the console. The token is now in scrollback.
```

### Expected

`RedactedIO().write(b"...hunter2...")` should produce the same masked output as `RedactedIO().write("...hunter2...")` — `...***...`.

### Actual

The bytes are passed to `redact()` first, and `redact()` does not understand `bytes` — they fall through `_redact`'s type checks to the default `return item` at [`secrets_masker.py:430`](https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/main/shared/secrets_masker/src/airflow_shared/secrets_masker/secrets_masker.py#L430), so the bytes object is returned unchanged. The `str(...)` wrapper in both `write()` ([line 720-722](https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/main/shared/secrets_masker/src/airflow_shared/secrets_masker/secrets_masker.py#L720)) and `writelines()` ([line 724-725](https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/main/shared/secrets_masker/src/airflow_shared/secrets_masker/secrets_masker.py#L724)) then converts the bytes to their `b'…'` repr, which writes the cleartext secret to the underlying stream.

### Why this matters

`RedactedIO` exists so that output produced by user code is masked before it reaches stdout. Its docstring says "Writes to stdout will be redacted." That promise is silently broken for the bytes path. Because the wrapper is applied to the entire task run, any user code that ever produces a `bytes` write through stdout is affected — and there's no error to warn the caller, the secret is just printed.

This was introduced into the `bytes` path of `writelines()` by #72063 (which deliberately propagated the behavior of the pre-existing `write()`). The `write()` method has had the same issue for a long time, but the only recently-added bytes-supporting code path is `writelines()`.

### Proposed fix

Decode `bytes`/`bytearray` to UTF-8 (with replacement) before calling `redact()` in both methods, so the existing pattern-based masker can see the content. Something like:

```python
def _redact_io_value(value) -> str:
    if isinstance(value, (bytes, bytearray)):
        value = value.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
    return str(redact(value))
```

Both `write()` and `writelines()` would call this helper, keeping them symmetric. The permissive behavior for non-string types is preserved (per the explicit intent of #72063), but bytes are now actually scanned for registered secrets.

### Area

- [x] secrets_masker
- [x] CLI (`airflow tasks test` is the only reachable production call site)

### Tested Airflow version

main (commit `935bac04f0`)

title: Remove the sqlalchemy<2.1 cap in the Snowflake provider once snowflake-sqlalchemy supports SQLAlchemy 2.1
body:
The Snowflake provider caps `sqlalchemy>=1.4.54,<2.1` (added in #73822, the CI environment upgrade).

**Why:** `snowflake-sqlalchemy` up to 1.11.1, the latest stable release, subclasses `sqlalchemy.orm.context.ORMSelectCompileState`. SQLAlchemy 2.1 renamed that class to the private `_ORMSelectCompileState`, so `import snowflake.sqlalchemy` fails, and with it `SnowflakeHook.get_uri()` and the OpenLineage URI extraction. The only newer release, the pre-release 2.0.0rc2, itself declares `sqlalchemy>=2.0.44,<2.1`. Because the uv workspace has a single resolution, the cap also keeps the whole CI environment and constraints on SQLAlchemy 2.0.x.

**Follow-up:**
- Once a `snowflake-sqlalchemy` release supports SQLAlchemy 2.1, raise the provider's `snowflake-sqlalchemy` floor to it and drop the `<2.1` cap in `providers/snowflake/pyproject.toml`.
- Regenerate `uv.lock` and check that the Snowflake hook tests (`test_hook_should_support_prepare_basic_conn_params_and_uri`) and `operators/test_sql.py::test_execute_openlineage_events` pass on SQLAlchemy 2.1.

**Done when:** the cap is removed and the Snowflake unit tests pass with SQLAlchemy 2.1 in the lock.

title: Marking a task success with include_future on a run without a logical date clears failed tasks in other runs
body:
### Under which category would you file this issue?

Airflow Core

### Apache Airflow version

3.3.2; also reproduced on main on October 19, 2026.

### What happened and how to reproduce it?

`PATCH /api/v2/dags/{dag_id}/dagRuns/{run_id}/taskInstances/{task_id}` with `{"new_state": "success", "include_future": true}` on a manually triggered run (no logical date) marks the task in that run only, but then clears the `failed`/`upstream_failed` downstream tasks of the Dag's other runs and sets those runs back to `queued`. The response lists only the target run, so the caller does not see it. `include_past` behaves the same, and so does the bulk `PATCH .../taskInstances` body. The clear route refuses this combination with 400 (#47036), and the Mark-as dialog disables Past and Future for such runs.

Dag file:

```python
import pendulum
from airflow.providers.standard.operators.bash import BashOperator
from airflow.providers.standard.operators.empty import EmptyOperator
from airflow.sdk import DAG

with DAG("probe", schedule=None, start_date=pendulum.datetime(2026, 1, 1, tz="UTC"), catchup=False):
    BashOperator(task_id="a", bash_command="exit 1", retries=0) >> EmptyOperator(task_id="b")
```

With `airflow standalone` running (LocalExecutor, SQLite, examples off), trigger two runs through the API: `dated` with `"logical_date": "2026-10-01T00:00:00+00:00"`, then `manual` with `"logical_date": null`. Once both have failed (`a` failed, `b` upstream_failed), run:

```sh
curl -s -X PATCH http://localhost:8080/api/v2/dags/probe/dagRuns/manual/taskInstances/a \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"new_state":"success","include_future":true}'
```

Result on 3.3.2 and main: the response is 200 and lists only `manual/a` as success, but the `dated` run also has `b` cleared and its state set to `queued`. Without `include_future`, or with it on the `dated` run, only the targeted run changes.

### What you think should happen instead?

A run without a logical date has no past or future. The request should either be rejected with the same 400 as the clear route, or affect that run alone, as the state change itself already does.

In `airflow-core/src/airflow/serialization/definitions/dag.py`, `SerializedDAG.set_task_instance_state` clears the downstream tasks with `start_date` (or `end_date`) set to the run's logical date; when that is `None`, no date bound is applied and the clear matches every run of the Dag. `set_task_group_state` has the same block, and the task-group route returns 500 for the same request (`DagRun.logical_date >= None` in its lock query).

### Operating System

macOS 26.2, Python 3.12 for 3.3.2; Linux/Breeze, Python 3.11 for main.

### Deployment

Virtualenv installation

### Versions of Apache Airflow Providers

`apache-airflow-providers-standard==1.19.0`

### Anything else?

No duplicate found in open/closed issue and PR searches for `include_future`, `include_past` and `set_task_instance_state`. #46804/#47036 cover the clear route only; #67707 and #63697 are about downstream tasks in the same run.

### Are you willing to submit PR?

No. I am reporting the bug and am not planning to submit a PR.

title: Scheduler does an unbounded DELETE on unreferenced triggers every cleanup tick
body:
### Summary

`SchedulerJobRunner._remove_unreferenced_triggers` issues an **unbounded single-statement `DELETE` against the `trigger` table every `parsing_cleanup_interval` (default 60s)**. On any deployment where the trigger table grows large — which is expected over time, since deferrable operators and asset/asset-alias watchers each leave a trigger row behind — this holds row locks for the entire transaction and stalls concurrent writers on the same table, including the triggerer's own `Trigger.clean_unused()` / `submit_event` paths. It also forces a full table materialisation in Python via `synchronize_session="fetch"` before the DELETE runs.

### Why this matters

- **AGENTS.md (Coding Standards) is explicit:** *"Bulk `DELETE`/`UPDATE` in the scheduler loop or any synchronous interval task (e.g. `call_regular_interval` callbacks) must be batched with `LIMIT` and committed between batches — never issue a single unbounded bulk write against a user-driven table. … Follow the batching pattern in `airflow-core/src/airflow/utils/db_cleanup.py`."* The current implementation predates and contradicts that rule. Affected column joins (`task_instance.trigger_id`, `asset_watcher.trigger_id`, `callback.trigger_id`) are already indexed.
- **Two cleanup paths, one batched and one not.** #70961 (merge commit `c3cc5573b8`) moved the **triggerer's** version (`Trigger.clean_unused()`) onto the existing pattern at `models/trigger.py:_delete_unused_batch`: `select id LIMIT, with_row_locks(skip_locked=True), delete by id, commit`, driven by `[triggerer] unreferenced_triggers_cleanup_batch_size`. The scheduler-side counterpart was missed by that change — only the triggerer's `clean_unused` callback in `jobs/triggerer_job_runner.py:clean_unused` was rewired. The scheduler still calls its own `_remove_unreferenced_triggers` from `jobs/scheduler_job_runner.py:2034`.

### Evidence

`airflow-core/src/airflow/jobs/scheduler_job_runner.py:4206-4219`:

```python
@provide_session
def _remove_unreferenced_triggers(self, *, session: Session = NEW_SESSION) -> None:
    """Remove triggers that are no longer used by anything."""
    session.execute(
        delete(Trigger)
        .where(
            ~exists(select(AssetWatcherModel.trigger_id).where(AssetWatcherModel.trigger_id == Trigger.id)),
            ~exists(select(Callback.trigger_id).where(Callback.trigger_id == Trigger.id)),
            ~exists(select(TaskInstance.trigger_id).where(TaskInstance.trigger_id == Trigger.id)),
        )
        .execution_options(synchronize_session="fetch")
    )
```

Existing tests are green at `airflow-core/tests/unit/jobs/test_scheduler_job.py:10051` and `:10087` (covering the unreferenced/referenced-path decision tree) but assume the unbounded form — they won't fail today because the table is small.

### Why I'm filing this

A previous PR — **#68241** "Batch the scheduler's unreferenced-trigger cleanup deletes" — implemented the same fix and was closed as a stale draft on 2026-07-02 (author inactive; `potiuk` moved it to draft because static / docs checks were failing). It would also re-roll the batching logic that already exists in `Trigger._delete_unused_batch`. **The triggerer side of this work landed (#70961); the scheduler side did not.**

### Proposed fix

Reuse the helper `Trigger._delete_unused_batch` from the scheduler rather than re-rolling the LIMIT/with_row_locks/commit-between-batches loop. Concretely:

1. Add a new config knob `[scheduler] unreferenced_triggers_cleanup_batch_size` (default `500`, `version_added: 3.3.0` per the existing `[triggerer]` option pattern).
2. Rewrite `_remove_unreferenced_triggers` to read that knob, validate it is `≥ 1`, and call `Trigger._delete_unused_batch(batch_size, session=session)`. The triggerer's `clean_unused` will keep the same cadence it has today (one batch per tick → drain over multiple ticks), so the net behaviour is the same modulo per-tick lock duration.
3. Extend tests in `tests/unit/jobs/test_scheduler_job.py` with: a batching-commit-count test (e.g. 5 triggers, `batch_size=2` → 3 commits), a non-positive-batch-size rejection test mirroring `tests/unit/models/test_trigger.py:325`, and a sanity test that referenced triggers survive.

### Areas

- area:scheduler
- area:core

### Reproduction

Hard to reproduce locally on a small fixture, but reproducible on any long-running install by tailing the scheduler logs for one cleanup tick after seeding N >> 500 unreferenced trigger rows; you will see the tick stretch to multiple seconds and any concurrent writer hitting `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` on `trigger` block.

### Airflow version

main at `7fbcfeea27` (post-#75096).

### Follow-ups

None expected — once the scheduler delegates to `Trigger._delete_unused_batch`, the cleanup pattern is fully owned by `Trigger`, and any future tuning (e.g. lock-skip policy, column-level WHERE tightening) edits one class.

title: Unable to create a mapped task group with a dynamic TriggerDagRunOperator trigger_dag_id
body:
### Under which category would you file this issue?

Providers

### Apache Airflow version

3.3.1

### What happened and how to reproduce it?

When writing an airflow dag using a mapped task group with TriggerDagOperator child tasks, setting the trigger_dag_id parameter on the TriggerDagOperator causes a serialization error on running `airflow dags reserialize` (notably the DAG parses successfully).

Example DAG:
```python
from datetime import datetime

from airflow.sdk import task_group, DAG
from airflow.operators.trigger_dagrun import TriggerDagRunOperator

with DAG(
    dag_id='expand_task_group_serialization_error',
    start_date=datetime(2026, 1, 1)
    schedule=None,
) as dag:
    @task_group(group_id="test_expanding_task_group")
    def trigger_one(dag_id):
        TriggerDagRunOperator(
            task_id="trigger",
            trigger_dag_id=dag_id
        )

    trigger_one.expand(dag_id=["dag_id_1", "dag_id_2"]
```

Loading the above code into the airflow DAGs directory and running `airflow dags reserialize` throws:
```
airflow.exceptions.SerializationError: Failed to serialize DAG 'expand_task_group_serialization_error': cannot use 'airflow.serialization.dag_dependency.DagDependency' as a set element (unhashable type: 'MappedArgument')
```

### What you think should happen instead?

Airflow should not throw the above error when serializing the DAG.
This looks to me like it's a result of the MappedArgument for trigger_dag_id passed from the expanded task group being used to create a DagDependency object. TriggerDagRunOperator.partial(...).expand(...) seems to automatically handle this case, as setting the trigger_dag_id as part of the expand call works fine there.
Whatever mechanism is in use there to avoid the DagDependency being created with an unserializable DAG ID should probably be replicated when a MappedArgument is passed directly to the constructor, but I wasn't able to find the code responsible for this.

A quick fix is to update the [DagDependency creation check](https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/main/airflow-core/src/airflow/serialization/serialized_objects.py#L912) to include a string typecheck on the trigger_dag_id, skipping the creation of the DagDependency entirely, but I'd rather keep the solution with whatever is in use for the existing TriggerDagRunOperator.partial(...).expand(...) method.

title: uv.lock on main fails to parse: duplicate package pyvespa==1.2.9
body:
### Description

`uv lock --check` (and `uv sync --frozen`) fails on a clean `main`:

```
error: Failed to parse `uv.lock`
  cause: Found duplicate package `pyvespa==1.2.9 @ registry+https://pypi.org/simple`
```

Reproduced with uv 0.12.18, 0.13.1 and 0.13.3 on `main` at `0a4b5d8e49` and
current `6aee277d4a` (macOS arm64). The `uv.lock` blob is
`eb0774d98a4571fd1a0359d8536d4b13aa41422b` (sha256
`cf8f72edaff55fa77a1ca03445032adf7e5b346f7c93154592408e5c2ac64014`); I copied
that exact blob from `git show upstream/main:uv.lock` into an isolated temp
directory and reproduced the parse failure with all three versions, so this is
not caused by the workspace or a local environment. `uv sync --frozen --project
airflow-core --group mypy --dry-run` fails with the same error.

### Cause

`uv.lock` is internally inconsistent after #73822:

- the two `pyvespa` package blocks were bumped from 1.2.7/1.2.9 to 1.2.9/1.2.9,
  so they are now identical except for `resolution-markers`, and uv reports the
  duplicate package;
- the resolved dependency graph for `apache-airflow-providers-vespa` still points
  at `pyvespa==1.2.7` for `python_version < '3.14'`, although no 1.2.7 package
  block exists anymore. After merging the duplicate blocks, uv then fails with
  `found dependency pyvespa==1.2.7 with no locked package`.

The provider still declares a split constraint:

```toml
# providers/vespa/pyproject.toml
"pyvespa>=1.2.9; python_version >= '3.14'",
"pyvespa>=1.1.2; python_version < '3.14'",
```

That constraint is not the problem: `pyvespa` 1.2.9 supports Python
`>=3.10,<3.16`, so both marker branches can resolve to 1.2.9. A fresh
`uv lock` with the same constraints produces a single 1.2.9 entry, and
replaying the 1.2.7→1.2.9 upgrade with uv 0.12.18, 0.13.1, 0.13.2 and 0.13.3
also dedupes correctly. This looks like a one-off inconsistent lock produced by
#73822 rather than a general resolver bug.

### Impact

Every `uv sync --frozen` on current `main` fails, so:

- prek hooks such as `mypy-*`, provider validation and `Update uv.lock` fail;
- CI jobs that sync the workspace fail (e.g. Airflow CTL tests 3.11–3.14,
  Scripts tests and Shared distributions tests on `0a4b5d8e49`);
- the merge ref for PR #75193 fails in Airflow CTL tests, Shared distributions
  tests and the CI image build with the same parse error;
- contributors cannot rebase/push branches onto current `main` without
  `--no-verify`.

### Suggested fix

#### Preferred minimal fix: partially revert the offending `pyvespa` hunk

For `pyvespa`, `#73822` changed only the `<3.14` package block: the version went
from 1.2.7 to 1.2.9, together with the `sdist` and wheel URLs/hashes. The
`apache-airflow-providers-vespa` dependency for `<3.14` was left pointing at
`pyvespa==1.2.7`, which is why the lock is inconsistent.

Restoring just that block to the parent (`0a4b5d8e49^`) content fixes the lock
without touching any other package:

- Python `<3.14`: `pyvespa==1.2.7` (allowed by the provider's `>=1.1.2`
  constraint)
- Python `>=3.14`: `pyvespa==1.2.9`
- `providers/vespa/pyproject.toml` is unchanged

The resulting diff is **3 insertions / 3 deletions**. `uv lock --check` passes
with uv 0.12.18, 0.13.1 and 0.13.3; `uv sync --frozen --project airflow-core
--group mypy --dry-run` passes; and running `uv lock` again makes no changes.
This is a targeted revert of the offending part of `#73822`, not a hand-invented
version. It does keep `pyvespa` at 1.2.7 for `<3.14`.

#### Alternative: regenerate the lock

If the intent is to keep `pyvespa` 1.2.9 for `<3.14` as well, regenerate
`uv.lock` with uv rather than hand-edit it. A fresh `uv lock` on current `main`
succeeds and produces a single `pyvespa==1.2.9` package block with no resolution
markers. `uv lock --check` passes with uv 0.13.1 and 0.13.3, and
`uv sync --frozen --project airflow-core --group mypy --dry-run` succeeds.

The generated lock differs from the current broken one by 803 changed lines
(441 insertions / 362 deletions). It contains 990 packages, with 40 package
names changed and one added (`google-cloud-sql`); examples of unrelated updates
include `pydantic-ai-slim` 2.56.0→2.57.0, `snowflake-connector-python`
5.0.0rc5→5.0.0 and several `google-cloud-*` packages. Starting from the last
valid lock (`0a4b5d8e49^`) and running `uv lock --upgrade` produces a
byte-identical lock, so this is the resolver's current canonical result, not an
artifact of deleting the file.

#### Emergency recovery: hand-repair the duplicate blocks

If a targeted partial revert or a full regeneration is not possible, the lock
can be hand-repaired as an emergency recovery:

1. merge the two `pyvespa==1.2.9` `[[package]]` blocks into one, dropping the
   redundant `resolution-markers`;
2. change the `< 3.14` resolved dependency of
   `apache-airflow-providers-vespa` from `pyvespa==1.2.7` to `pyvespa==1.2.9`.

With these two edits, `uv lock --check` passes with uv 0.13.1 and 0.13.3,
`uv sync --frozen --project airflow-core --group mypy --dry-run` passes, and the
lock diff is 1 insertion / 47 deletions. This is a recovery for the unparseable
file, not the normal generated workflow, and should only be used if the larger
regeneration diff is not acceptable.

The provider constraint does not need to change in any case.

### Environment

- uv 0.13.3 (also reproduced with 0.12.18 and 0.13.1)
- macOS arm64; repo venv CPython 3.12.15, isolated probe used CPython 3.14.7
  selected by uv
- `uv.lock` revision 5, `requires-python >=3.11`

Related: #73822, #75062

title: Improve the overall static check speed
body:
### Body

The current static check full run (including all the prek hooks, mypy, ruff, etc) takes over 20 minutes, we should improve them for sure.

Here're some stages to improve the overall speed:

0. Benchmark the all steps in the static check so far
1. Parallelize the check as workaround. We need to make sure they won't conflict or there won't be any side effect when run them in parallel. Additionally, we need to group the steps properly for the speedup purpose, packing those fast hooks doesn't make sense.
2. Move some of those hooks as unit test. IIRC, some of those hooks are unnecessary as "prek hook" and them should be moved as static check
3. Improve some of those expensive prek hooks individually
4. Add the monitor / alert for the entire static check in `#internal-ci-cd-channel` to avoid introducing bad practice in the future (just like the k8s test alerts)

title: Skip log accumulator on NDJSON reads of running task logs
body:
Follow-up to #70671.

`FileTaskHandler._read` wraps reads of a running task in `LogStreamAccumulator` to count lines for `log_pos`. The accumulator drains the whole log, to memory and then to a temp file, before the first line is returned.

The NDJSON path of `GET /dags/{dag_id}/dagRuns/{dag_run_id}/taskInstances/{task_id}/logs/{try_number}` never uses that `log_pos`:

- `get_log` builds the `Airflow-Continuation-Token` header from the inbound metadata before `read_log_stream` runs.
- `read_log_stream` pops any inbound `log_pos` before reading.

NDJSON is the UI's default `accept`, so a running task open in the UI drains its whole log on every refresh.

### Proposal

Let the caller say whether it needs `log_pos`, instead of inferring it from `end_of_log`. Only the JSON branch of `get_log` turns `log_pos` into a continuation token, so only that branch asks for the count. The NDJSON path then streams running task logs lazily, like finished ones.

title: Clear task confirmation dialog reopens without clearing the task
body:
### Under which category would you file this issue?

Airflow Core

### Apache Airflow version

3.4.0b1; also reproduced on main

### What happened and how to reproduce it?

Clicking **Confirm** in the **Clear Task Instance** dialog causes it to briefly disappear and reopen. The selected task is not cleared or rerun, and its try number remains unchanged.

I reproduced this on main and in a separate deployment using the official `apache/airflow:3.4.0b1` image. I observed the behavior in both Safari and Chrome.

### Reproduction Dag

```python
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from time import sleep

from airflow.sdk import DAG, task

with DAG(
    dag_id="reproduce_clear_task_dialog",
    schedule=None,
    start_date=datetime(2026, 1, 1, tzinfo=timezone.utc),
    catchup=False,
    tags=["reproduction", "clear-dialog"],
) as dag:

    @task
    def wait_seconds(seconds: int):
        sleep(seconds)

    a = wait_seconds.override(task_id="A")(3)
    b = wait_seconds.override(task_id="B")(30)
    c = wait_seconds.override(task_id="C")(3)

    a >> b >> c
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. Deploy the Dag, enable it, and trigger a run.
2. Wait until A, B, and C have succeeded.
3. Open the completed run's Task Instances tab.
4. Click the clear action for task C.
5. Ensure only C is selected. Leave Past, Future, Upstream, Downstream, and Clear only failed tasks unselected.
6. Leave **Prevent rerun if task is running** checked and **Keep task state and resume** unchecked.
7. Click **Confirm**.

### Actual result

The dialog flickers and reopens instead of completing the clear action. Task C remains successful with its original try number.

In the captured failed interactions, requests to
`POST /api/v2/dags/{dag_id}/clearTaskInstances` return HTTP 200 with
`dry_run: true` in their request payloads. No request with `dry_run: false`
was observed.

The attached recording shows the dialog behavior, a request payload with
`dry_run: true`, and the unchanged try number afterward.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a050ca19-d1a6-417b-89af-20d5c80b06ae

### What you think should happen instead?

Confirming the clear action should send the actual clear request and close the dialog after it succeeds. With the scheduler running and dependencies satisfied, task C should rerun and its try number should increase.

### Operating System

macOS host, with Airflow running in Linux Docker containers.

### Deployment

Docker-Compose

### Apache Airflow Provider(s)

_No response_

### Versions of Apache Airflow Providers

_No response_

Not Applicable

_No response_

_No response_

The beta reproduction used the official apache/airflow:3.4.0b1 image with a mounted reproduction Dag and local configuration. Main was tested using Breeze.

### Anything else?

Sending a clear request directly with dry_run: false successfully reruns the task.

The behavior was observed in both Safari and Chrome. The attached recording shows the failed UI interaction and a request payload containing dry_run: true.

title: Scheduler crashes on every restart when a scheduled task with a task concurrency limit belongs to a Dag that no longer deserializes
body:
### Under which category would you file this issue?

Airflow Core

### Apache Airflow version

3.3.2; also reproduced on main on October 20, 2026.

### What happened and how to reproduce it?

When a Dag stops deserializing (for example a custom timetable whose `deserialize` reads a Variable that was deleted) and one of its tasks is in `scheduled` with `max_active_tis_per_dag` or `max_active_tis_per_dagrun` set, the scheduler exits with an uncaught `DeserializationError` on its first loop after a restart, and again on every restart. Every other Dag stops being scheduled until that task is cleared or the Dag loads again. #74499 fixed the same crash for a queued run of such a Dag; a running run with a scheduled task still has it.

Plugin (`plugins/probe_timetable.py`): a timetable that fails to deserialize once a flag file is gone, standing in for one that reads a missing Variable.

```python
import os

from airflow.plugins_manager import AirflowPlugin
from airflow.timetables.base import DataInterval, Timetable


class FlagTimetable(Timetable):
    def infer_manual_data_interval(self, *, run_after):
        return DataInterval(run_after, run_after)

    def next_dagrun_info(self, *, last_automated_data_interval, restriction):
        return None

    def serialize(self):
        return {}

    @classmethod
    def deserialize(cls, data):
        if not os.path.exists(os.environ["PROBE_FLAG"]):
            raise ValueError("flag missing, cannot deserialize FlagTimetable")
        return cls()


class ProbeTimetablePlugin(AirflowPlugin):
    name = "probe_timetable"
    timetables = [FlagTimetable]
```

Dag file:

```python
from airflow.providers.standard.operators.bash import BashOperator
from airflow.sdk import DAG
from probe_timetable import FlagTimetable

with DAG("probe_bad_long", schedule=FlagTimetable(), catchup=False):
    BashOperator(task_id="t1", bash_command="sleep 600", max_active_tis_per_dag=1)
```

With `PROBE_FLAG` pointing at an existing file and `airflow standalone` running (LocalExecutor, SQLite, examples off, Dags unpaused at creation), trigger two runs of `probe_bad_long` through the API. Run 1's `t1` starts; run 2's `t1` stays `scheduled` behind `max_active_tis_per_dag=1`. Then stop everything, delete the flag file, and start the scheduler alone:

```sh
rm "$PROBE_FLAG"
airflow scheduler --num-runs 8; echo "exit $?"
```

Result on 3.3.2 and main: the scheduler logs "Error scheduling DAG run r2 of probe_bad_long" (and r1) with the `ValueError`, and skips those runs as expected, then exits with code 1 from `_task_concurrency_allows_execution`:

```
  File ".../airflow/jobs/scheduler_job_runner.py", line 932, in _select_task_instances_to_queue
    self._task_concurrency_allows_execution(
  File ".../airflow/jobs/scheduler_job_runner.py", line 615, in _task_concurrency_allows_execution
    serialized_dag = self.scheduler_dag_bag.get_dag_for_run(
  ...
airflow.exceptions.DeserializationError: An unexpected error occurred while trying to deserialize Dag 'probe_bad_long'
```

Run 2's `t1` is still `scheduled`, so starting the scheduler again exits the same way. With the flag file back, the same command finishes its loops and queues `t1`. The same Dag without `max_active_tis_per_dag` only gets the "Error scheduling DAG run" log and the scheduler keeps going, because the task concurrency check is the only place on this path that loads the Dag again.

### What you think should happen instead?

Log the error and skip the task, as `_schedule_all_dag_runs` does for the run and as #74499 made `_start_queued_dagruns` do for queued runs, so one Dag that no longer loads does not stop every other Dag from being scheduled.

In `airflow-core/src/airflow/jobs/scheduler_job_runner.py`, `_task_concurrency_allows_execution` calls `scheduler_dag_bag.get_dag_for_run` without catching the deserialization error; it is called from `_select_task_instances_to_queue` for every scheduled task whose Dag has a task concurrency limit, and the error propagates out of the scheduler loop.

### Operating System

macOS 26.2, Python 3.12 for 3.3.2; Linux/Breeze, Python 3.11 for main.

### Deployment

Virtualenv installation

### Versions of Apache Airflow Providers

`apache-airflow-providers-standard==1.19.0`

### Anything else?

No duplicate found in open/closed issue and PR searches for "scheduler crash deserialize", "DeserializationError scheduler", "max_active_tis_per_dag crash", "timetable deserialize Variable" and `_task_concurrency_allows_execution`. #62050/#72243 are about the same function when the serialized Dag row is missing (it returns `None`), not when deserialization raises. #54771 is a different deserialization failure.

### Are you willing to submit PR?

No. I am reporting the bug and am not planning to submit a PR.

### Code of Conduct

- [x] I agree to follow this project's [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
